survivors.claim: The fix introduces an unconditional 2 s sleep (await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2000))) before asserting the notes-event count, so the test always takes at least 2 s longer regardless of how fast the event arrives; deterministic (not flaky) and well inside the 20 s test timeout, but a fixed wall-clock cost rather than an early-exit-on-settle window.
survivors.impact: The API test file is a couple of seconds slower on every run; the wait cannot cause a false failure, only extra time.
survivors.evidence: Executed: npx vitest run tests/server/api.test.ts -t AC-20260918-01-7 --reporter=verbose -> passed in 3541 ms (whole file 29/29 passed, 51.99 s); three consecutive isolated runs all passed. The AC says within 2 s, so the 2 s window is the spec own number; the only cost is that the window never closes early.

survivors.claim: The exactly-one-notes-event count observes what the watcher delivers, and the file watcher coalesces two rapid writes to design/notes.json into one event; the assertion therefore pins one POST -> one event (and would catch a double emit per change in watch.ts, which emits directly with no debounce for notes) but cannot pin one-event-per-write when writes land inside the watcher coalescing window.
survivors.impact: The test proves the single-write case the acceptance criterion describes; it cannot, with this watcher, prove per-write counting for back-to-back writes. Advisory context, not a defect in the fix.
survivors.evidence: Executed scratch vitest (created under tests/server/, deleted afterwards): identical counting loop, two POST notes op=add back-to-back -> NOTES_EVENTS_AFTER_TWO_POSTS 1; two POSTs spaced 700 ms apart -> count 2 (expect(count).toBe(2) passed). src/server/watch.ts:39-40: if (file === notesPath) { emit(notes) } - no debounce on the notes path, so a duplicate emit in our code would be counted.
